page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.u1 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon core operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not feature local storage or GPU acceleration, relying on external network storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the instance delivers average single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1843.79 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1371.0. However, multi-core and memory subsystem performance are limited. The stress-ng multi-core test yielded 1921.48, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 1586.0, both falling into the lower performance percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measured at 14.71 GB/sec and 13.41 GB/sec respectively.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.u1-c1m4.large is positioned as a cost-efficient option for entry-level workloads that do not require high parallel processing power or intensive memory throughput. It is suitable for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic web serving, small-scale Redis deployments, and development or testing environments. The lack of local storage and moderate network bandwidth make it less ideal for high-volume database operations or data-intensive ETL pipelines.

The instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight workloads, such as basic web serving, development environments, and small-scale background processing tasks where resource demands are modest and cost efficiency is prioritized over high-throughput performance.
